To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increasing EC of nutrient solution reduces tomato growth and photosynthetic rate but does not affect dry matter content or photosynthetic rate of individual leaves.
increasing EC reduced plant growth and whole plant photosynthesis but did not decrease dry weight and leaf area, and that increasing PPF enhanced growth and photosynthesis.
increasing nutrient solution concentration reduced tomato growth and photosynthetic response to PPF, but it did not reduce leaf photosynthetic response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of nutrient solution EC on growth and leaf photosynthesis of tomato plants.
the effects of increasing nutrient solution concentration (EC) on tomato growth and photosynthetic response.
the question of whether an increase in EC to produce high quality fruit vegetables, such the tomato, reduces growth and yield.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an increase in EC reduced plant growth and photosynthesis in a dose-dependent way.
an increase in EC of nutrient solution reduces growth and photosynthesis, and that this effect can be partially compensated by increasing PPF.
the growth and photosynthesis response of whole tomato plants to nutrient solution concentration depends on light level, and that the effect of increasing EC on growth and photosynthesis is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
an increase in nutrient solution EC reduced growth and photosynthesis, but not to a degree that would reduce fruit quality.
increasing EC reduced growth and photosynthesis, but not to the point that it would be a limiting factor for production of high quality tomatoes.
an increase in nutrient solution EC reduced growth and whole plant photosynthesis, but did not reduce leaf photosynthesis and leaf dry matter content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photosynthesis and growth of tomato plants are reduced by increasing nutrient solution EC, and that the decrease in plant dry matter is due to reduced leaf area.
increasing EC in nutrient solutions to enhance tomato fruit quality does not decrease plant growth, and that photosynthetic inhibition does not appear to be a factor.
nutrient solution EC can be increased without reducing photosynthesis and growth, provided that PPF is high enough.
